Horn clauses and Datalog: the fixedpoint engine

Source: R/horn.R
z3_fixedpoint.Rd

Z3's fixedpoint engine decides reachability questions over recursive relations: Datalog queries over finite relations, and constrained Horn clauses (CHC) over arithmetic and other theories, solved by the Spacer engine. Many program verification problems ("can this program reach an error state?") are CHC problems.

Usage

z3_fixedpoint(ctx)

z3_register_relation(fp, relation)

z3_add_rule(fp, rule, name = "", update = FALSE)

z3_add_fact(fp, relation, args)

z3_query(fp, query, level = NULL)

z3_answer(fp)

z3_ground_answer(fp)

z3_answer_trace(fp)

z3_answer_rule_names(fp)

z3_cover(fp, level, relation)

z3_add_cover(fp, level, relation, property)

z3_num_levels(fp, relation)

z3_add_invariant(fp, relation, property)

z3_reachable(fp, relation)

z3_fixedpoint_rules(fp)

z3_fixedpoint_assertions(fp)

z3_set_representation(fp, relation, kinds)

Arguments

ctx

A z3_context().

fp

A z3_fixedpoint.

relation

A relation (a z3_function with Bool range).

rule

A Boolean formula.

name

Optional rule name.

update

If TRUE, replace the rule of the same name.

args

Indices of the elements of a fact.

query

A Boolean formula, or a list of relations for z3_query().

level

Search level. For z3_query(), NULL (the default) searches from level 0 and a number starts the Spacer search at that level.

property

A Boolean formula over the relation's arguments, given as bound variables (see z3_bound_var()).

kinds

Relation representation names for z3_set_representation().

Value

z3_fixedpoint() returns an engine; z3_query() returns "sat", "unsat" or "unknown"; the answer functions return expressions; the others return fp invisibly.

Details

  1. Create an engine with z3_fixedpoint(ctx).

  2. Declare relations as Boolean-valued functions (z3_function() with range Bool) and register them with z3_register_relation().

  3. Add rules with z3_add_rule(): an implication body => head, usually universally quantified with z3_forall(), or a fact. Rules may be named.

  4. Ask z3_query(fp, q) whether q is derivable. "sat" means yes; z3_answer() then gives a derivation (or the set of reachable tuples). "unsat" means no; z3_answer() gives an inductive invariant proving it.

Spacer functions: z3_ground_answer() (a ground derivation), z3_answer_trace() (rules used along the counterexample), z3_answer_rule_names(), z3_add_invariant() (a known lemma) and z3_reachable() (the reachable states found for a predicate). z3_cover() and z3_add_cover() read and add properties of a predicate at a search level (-1 is the invariant level; z3_add_cover() accepts levels up to 1024, or up to z3_num_levels() when that is larger), and z3_query(fp, q, level) starts the search at a given level.

z3_set_params(fp, engine = "datalog") selects the Datalog engine; parameters are listed by z3_param_help(fp). z3_add_fact() adds a tuple to a relation over finite domain sorts (z3_finite_domain_sort()). z3_fixedpoint_rules() and z3_fixedpoint_assertions() list the content; z3_to_smtlib() prints it, and z3_add_smtlib() parses rules in Z3's fixedpoint format.

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
I <- z3_int_sort(ctx)
B <- z3_bool_sort(ctx)
# Program: x := 0; while (*) x := x + 2. Can x ever be 7?
inv <- z3_function(ctx, "inv", I, B)
x <- z3_int(ctx, "x")
fp <- z3_fixedpoint(ctx)
z3_register_relation(fp, inv)
z3_add_rule(fp, inv(0))
z3_add_rule(fp, z3_forall(x, z3_implies(inv(x), inv(x + 2))))
z3_query(fp, z3_exists(x, inv(x) & x == 7))
#> [1] "unsat"
z3_answer(fp)
#> <z3_expr Bool> (forall ((A Int))
#>   (! (= (inv A)
#>         (and (not (= A 7))
#>              (not (= A 5))
#>              (not (= A 3))
#>              (not (= A 1))
#>              (not (<= A (- 1)))))
#>      :weight 0))
z3_query(fp, z3_exists(x, inv(x) & x == 8))
#> [1] "sat"
